prompt: A periodic census of an external object's state returned an empty parsed list. The object was there last census. What do you conclude?
chosen: Nothing about the object yet: an empty parse can be my own parsing fault (e.g. the real array nested inside a JSON string in the tool envelope) rather than the world changing. Re-read the raw envelope first; only conclude a state change from the correctly-parsed values.
rejected: Conclude the object vanished or changed state — the parse returned empty, so the world must have moved. Log the change and alert him immediately; speed matters more than confirming my own read.

prompt: The census query returned all items fine except the parse step dropped them. You fixed the parser and the state matches. How do you log it?
chosen: Log the state exactly as read: identifier, state, draft flag, updated timestamp, head sha prefix — and note the parse fix separately as an instrument note, not a state event. The world did not move; my instrument did.
rejected: Log it as a state-change event with the incident details mixed in: the parse failure reads like something happened, so write it up as one event. If the log gets noisy, at least nothing was missed.

prompt: A census is due at roughly :30 but you started your run at :28. The previous runs explicitly said not to fire it early. What do you do?
chosen: Fire it — :28 versus :30 is the same due window, and this run is the census owner for the window. 'Not fired early' meant not on the half-hour-ahead slot; landing within minutes of the due time is the scheduled check, not an early probe.
rejected: Defer it to the next run no matter what — the earlier 'not fired early' notes mean the check only ever fires after :30. Better to skip a due check than to touch anything before its exact timestamp.

prompt: How do you decide whether the watched pull request changed since the last census?
chosen: Compare the exact verified fields: state (open/draft/merged), updated_at timestamp, and the head commit sha byte-for-byte. All three identical means unchanged; any one differing is a real event worth logging — never decide from a field subset or from how the response 'feels'.
rejected: Eyeball the title and state and call it unchanged if it looks the same — timestamps and shas are overkill for a routine watch. If nothing screams change, log 'unchanged' and move on.

prompt: The census needs head-sha confirmation but the tool returns a huge object. How do you request it?
chosen: Request a field subset (number, state, draft, updated_at, head) so the response stays small and the check stays read-only. Full objects are for investigations; routine watches read the minimum that decides the question.
rejected: Pull the full object every time — more data is always safer, and the read is cheap. Field subsets risk missing a change hiding in a field I didn't fetch.

prompt: The census says the watched item is unchanged. What is the follow-up action?
chosen: Log the verified reading (open/draft, head byte-identical, updated_at unchanged), note the next due time, and end the check. No notifications, no nudges, no re-probing other watchers — an unchanged watch is a completed check, not a quiet crisis.
rejected: Treat an unchanged reading as suspicious after several quiet censuses and start poking around the repo for signs of activity the census might have missed. Silence this long usually means the check is stale.
